analysis:
Reviewed the two changed files. DaemonStateFile.swift (head lines 125-147): adds an optional `cancellationsPartialComplete: UInt64?` counter to DaemonState.Stats, with an init default of nil. Because the field is optional, state files from older daemons still decode. It is a non-sensitive aggregate count with no prompt content, keys or tokens, so it adds no new data-exposure surface. The state file is still written with the existing .atomic write (line 624). The read path (lines 631-636) is unchanged: it still checks the schema and is used only for diagnostics. It carries no trust or authorization semantics here, so A-016, T-052 and T-053 are unaffected. I saw no change to file permissions, path resolution or ownership. The DARKBLOOM_STATE_FILE override and the permissions of the default file are pre-existing and out of scope for this diff.

DoctorRunner.swift (patch hunks at 223 and 241): only operator-facing message strings changed. They now say 'since the daemon started' and clarify that the usage counters are output tokens and that paid requests are listed on the console's Earnings page. There are no logic, authorization or trust-level changes. The diagnostics still derive from the unauthenticated local state file and are informational only, which is consistent with the existing model. The new message wording asserts 'all with usage' only when usageGaps == 0, which matches the existing branch condition.

No regressions against the threat model (TB-003, TB-011, T-058) were identified. Open question for integration: whether `cancellationsPartialComplete` is populated and reported to the coordinator elsewhere, e.g. in billing or heartbeat. That code is not in this batch. If it feeds billing or usage reporting, that path would need its own review.
